page: Amazon Web Services g5.8xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture, combining general-purpose compute capacity with hardware-accelerated processing. The instance provides 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz. Memory capacity stands at 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A dedicated NVIDIA A10G GPU with 22 GB of VRAM is included directly in the hardware configuration, alongside a bundled 900 GB local NVMe SSD and 25 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Empirical benchmark measurements show distinct performance specialization across compute layers. CPU metrics indicate modest single-thread performance, with stress-ng single-core in the bottom 10% and Geekbench single-core reaching 1335.0. Multi-core performance aligns with the middle tier, delivering a Geekbench multi-core score of 11223.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 34661.31. In contrast, the dedicated GPU delivers top-tier throughput in language model execution, registering 9419.27 prompt tokens per second on small 135M models and 2889.44 prompt tokens per second on medium 7B models, both falling within the top 10% tier. Memory subsystem operations also demonstrate strength, with PassMark memory scoring in the top 25%.

The integration of local NVMe storage with 22 GB of GPU memory offers operational efficiency for IOPS-sensitive machine learning pipelines without incurring the latency of remote block storage. While CPU-bound serial processing remains a tradeoff, the dense combination of 32 threads, 128 GB memory, and high inference throughput establishes g5.8xlarge as an effective platform for deep learning inference, model serving, video transcoding, and graphics rendering.
description: Amazon Web Services g5.8xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro System, integrating a 32-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R32 processor clocked at 3.3 GHz with 128 GB of DDR4 memory. The hardware configuration bundles an NVIDIA A10G Tensor Core GPU with 22 GB of VRAM alongside a 900 GB local NVMe SSD and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data reflects moderate CPU throughput, with mid-tier multi-core results, paired with top-tier machine learning inference speeds on models up to 7B parameters. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio and dedicated local NVMe storage deliver balanced system throughput without relying solely on remote volumes. Given the GPU acceleration profile and balanced system resources, g5.8xlarge is suited for graphics rendering, video transcoding, and deep learning inference pipelines.
